Subject: Post-call: Streaming UX & Concurrency Targets — next steps

Hi Taylor / Samir —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Quick recap of what I captured and the recommended next steps so we all stay aligned. Please flag anything I got wrong.

Summary of pain and goals
- Current pain: unpredictable late-stage checkout recommender latency spikes during promotions (30–40% of requests exceed acceptable UX window).
- Measured baseline: p95 response ~820ms for single-stream generation at current model; bursts push p99 >> 2s.
- Business goal: p95 <= 250ms for the majority of interactive flows, and streaming token latency per-frame experience <= 150ms for real-time previews.
- Throughput requirement: sustained 1,200 reqs/minute with spiky bursts to 4,500 rpm during peak promotions (10–15 minute windows).

Current stack
- Frontend: React-based streaming UI that renders incremental tokens.
- Backend: in-house API that fans out requests to a model cluster (owners: infra team).
- Models: fine-tuned open Llama variant (quantized). No KV caching in front of model today.

Success criteria (what success looks like for Acme)
- p95 generation <= 250ms under normal traffic; degraded-but-usable behavior during spikes with graceful fallbacks.
- Streaming UX: first token < 100ms, subsequent token steady-state < 150ms.
- Clear cost/throughput tradeoffs documented so you can choose reserved vs burst capacity.

Immediate next steps (we agreed on these)
1) Redwood to run quick profiling on your sample payloads to validate p95/p99 targets and recommend batching/caching knobs — deliverable: short report + recommended config (due: Aug 6).
2) Acme to share anonymized sample logs (same format as today) and promotion-day traffic pattern (CSV). Samir to send by EOD Wed Aug 4.
3) Align on an SLO-runbook: fallback model variants, region routing, and a canary plan for a two-week pilot (owners: Diego + Acme infra).
4) Schedule a tech deep-dive next week (30–45m) to go through profiling output and rollout plan.

Attachments: I attached a short SLA worksheet with p95 mapping and a sample cost estimate for dedicated capacity vs burst.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Nice capture. Two quick notes from the infra side before profiling:
1) We'll want samples at both quantized and FP16 flavors if they have them — quantized often lowers cost but can add token variance that affects p95. Ask Samir to include model meta if possible.
2) For profiling, we should run three experiments: single-request latency, batched throughput at target QPS, and streaming-first-token latency with a synthetic keepalive to simulate UI rendering. I can spin up the harness and run the tests if we have the CSV by Wed.

I'll also draft a short canary checklist (auto-scale thresholds, cold-start limits, and an abort criteria for rollback).
